q: How do I estimate the carbon footprint of a forged crankshaft?
title: Forged crankshaft carbon footprint
short: Start with the steel bar mass bought, not the finished weight, since forging flash and machining remove a large share. Multiply by the steel supplier's CO2 per tonne, then add forging furnace fuel, heat treatment and machining electricity per piece.
audience: Auto component forgers and machine shops

ul: Bar weight per piece, from the cut length.
Steel supplier's CO2 per tonne, with its date.
Furnace fuel and electricity per piece from monthly bills and output.

p: Flash and turnings sold as scrap leave with your waste. Do not subtract them from the steel bought unless you follow a stated recycling method.

example.title: Worked example (illustrative figures)
lines: Supplier figure: 2.2 kg CO2 per kg of steel; 20 × 2.2 = 44 kg.
Forging, heat treatment and machining: 6 kWh × 0.710 (FY 2024-25 grid factor) = 4.3 kg, plus 1.5 kg from furnace gas.
Total: about 50 kg CO2 per piece.

senseible: Senseible reads your electricity bills, fuel invoices and purchase invoices into dated, fingerprinted records, so a per unit footprint can be traced back to the documents behind it. Estimates are labelled as estimates.
